review_basis: The third entry off opentakeoff-corpus/reports/LINEAR_HELDOUT.txt's frozen list -- this exact sheet (navfac-cherry-point-atc-mechanical.pdf#6, MH101) was one of that file's own TWO coordinator-chosen sheets, picked STRUCTURALLY (first sheet in the PDF's own MH series) before any trace_run call was made against it, so authoring a golden here now carries no engine-behavior selection bias. Candidate found via a grid-sweep of trace_run seeds near this sheet's own explicit duct-size labels (a much cleaner search than the two prior held-out sheets: every duct callout here already carries its own direct SA/RA/EA system tag, e.g. '8x8 RA', '16/12 SA', '12x10 EA' -- no system-code inference needed, unlike weld-county's or itd-p4's disclosed circumstantial reasoning). The chosen run (8x8 RA, 12.39 LF) reads systems:['RA'] directly from trace_run itself, not annotator inference. A marked render crop (session.viewSheet with ring marks at both endpoints) confirms both ends sit on genuine drawn CAD geometry: the near end (2664.7,1046.9, stop reason 'ambiguous') sits exactly at a real hatched transition/flex-connector fitting where this duct meets a vertical riser; the far end (2887.7,1046.9, stop reason 'ambiguous') sits exactly at a real elbow turning up into a register/riser connection near an 'RG-' (return grille) tag -- both real forks (the walker could continue in more than one direction at each), not narrative stops, the same 'ambiguous, not dead_end' pattern the plan's own §6.3 design anticipates. No named PDF OCG layer exists on this sheet for M-prefixed names (session.sheetInfo()'s own layer list confirmed empty) -- like federal-m41-hhws-pump-stub and itd-p4-ea-duct-stub, this reads confidence:0 / 'stroke-family:unclassified' / 'layer-unclassified', the same lower-confidence code path as those two, not weld-county's cleaner layer-name read. This sheet is considerably denser than the other held-out sheets (53,534 segments) -- several nearby seed sweeps near other size labels on the same sheet landed in tightly-clustered fitting details with sub-1LF reaches and undefined sizes (too small/ambiguous to trust as a clean golden), consistent with this sheet's own real visual density; this candidate was chosen specifically because it sits in a comparatively open, uncluttered run of duct between two identifiable fittings, confirmed by the marked crop showing clean space on both sides of the traced span.
scope: The third entry in opentakeoff-corpus/reports/LINEAR_HELDOUT.txt's frozen split (federal-attachment4-mechanical.pdf#7 and itd-d1-lab-mechanical.pdf#4 are already authored). This run is an 8x8 rectangular return-air (RA) duct segment on a dense airport-tower mechanical ductwork plan, from a real transition/flex-connector fitting to a real elbow into a register riser. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the vertical ducts at both ends (up toward 'M41'/FCU-A1, down toward the unrelated '12/8 SA' VAV-A113 branch); every other duct run on this visually dense sheet (dozens of SA/RA/EA branches feeding VAV boxes, FCUs, and terminal registers across the plan); the second remaining navfac coordinator pick (navfac-cherry-point-atc-mechanical.pdf#18, MP101, still declared but unauthored); the other 4 remaining declared-but-unauthored held-out sheets (baker-county-eoc-bidset.pdf#38, bldg5406-hvac-demo-mechanical.pdf#2/#14).
